title: Resolve per-model usage drift in Console after delayed backfill & quota throttling
creator: Ravi Kothari
description:
Problem summary:
Console charts for usage (per-model token breakdowns and hourly ingestion graphs) have been showing persistent undercounts for a subset of customers over the last 72 hours. The billing backend reports token counts that do not match Console totals (diffs up to 18% for some models). Investigations show discrepancies are concentrated on: (1) streaming responses and server-side quotas that returned 429 truncations, and (2) delayed backfilled events from the ingestion pipeline (daily ETL backfills) not tagging model_variant correctly. Both cause per-model attribution to be wrong and charts to show drift after backfill windows.

Key impact: inaccurate per-model usage breakdowns in Console, confusing customers and potentially leading to billing disputes. Needs deterministic fix and one-time reprocess of affected partitions plus new monitoring to avoid recurrence.
root_cause_analysis: Ingest pipeline (kinesis -> raw_events -> hourly_aggregator) incorrectly drops 'model_variant' when events are produced by the streaming gateway because the streaming producer emits 'model' but not 'model_variant' in the legacy envelope; aggregator fallback logic used 'model' only for non-backfill runs leading to attribution ambiguity.

Quota/throttling paths returned partial responses with ‘request_status=throttled’ but still emitted token estimates to billing pipeline; Console consumer has a dedup + filter that excludes throttled events resulting in undercount in dashboard while billing counts include them.

Backfill runner that rewrites older raw_event partitions in S3 used a different schema version (v2.1) which the hourly_aggregator was not configured to parse for 'model_variant' — backfilled partitions therefore recorded as 'unknown' in the per-model table.
There is no alerting for ingestion lag greater than 6 hours; backfills can take 12–36 hours without on-call visibility.
proposed_solution: Short-term (hotfix): Update hourly_aggregator to merge 'model' + 'model_variant' using a deterministic mapping table for streaming envelopes; include throttled events by default (with 'throttled' flag) so Console and billing see consistent raw counts.

One-time backfill: Run a safe reprocess job for affected S3 partitions (2026-03-01 to 2026-03-09) with schema-aware parser (v2.1) and materialize corrected per_model_hourly aggregates into the analytics table, while tagging rows with 'reprocessed=true' for traceability.

Monitoring & guardrails: Add an alert (pager) when hourly ingestion lag > 6 hours; add a dashboard panel showing percent of tokens with unknown model_variant and a daily summary email to PM/ops during rollout window.

Data correctness: Add E2E assertion job that compares billing tokens (from billing-aggregates) vs console_tokens (from analytics per_model_hourly) and fails if difference > 0.5% for high-volume customers.
UX: Console should show an annotation on charts for 'backfill in progress' and once reprocess completes show a 'backfilled' tooltip with link to ticket and reprocess PR.
acceptance_criteria: Per-model hourly charts in Console match billing-aggregates token counts within 0.5% for a sample of 20 high-volume customers for the reprocess window.
Reprocess job runs to completion for 2026-03-01..2026-03-09 and creates rows with reprocessed=true.
New ingestion lag alert fires correctly in staging when lag is simulated > 6 hours and not noisy in normal operation.
Console displays a backfill annotation during reprocessing and removes it when done; tooltip contains PR link and ticket key.
QA sign-off from Billing (Aria team) and Console PM (Lead: Priya Desai).
tasks: ENG: Add schema-aware parser and deterministic model_variant mapping in hourly_aggregator (PR: github.com/redwood/ingest/pull/1284)
ENG: Implement inclusion of throttled events in analytics path (toggle behind feature flag: include_throttled_events)
ENG: Author and run reprocess job with small window in staging -> validate -> run in prod (S3 partitions 2026-03-01..2026-03-09)
ENG/PM: Add Console UI annotation and backfill status panel (design: confluence.redwood.ai/display/CONSOLE/Backfill+UX)
SRE: Add PagerDuty alert & dashboard panel for ingestion lag > 6h and percent_unknown_model_variant
QA: Smoke test token parity check and per-model chart correctness, produce audit log samples for 5 customers
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Reprocessing large S3 partitions may temporarily increase load on aggregator and DB. Mitigation: throttle reprocess to 1 partition/minute, run during low-traffic window (01:00-06:00 UTC) and run a canary on a single customer first.

Risk: Including throttled events could change customer-visible charts unexpectedly. Mitigation: feature-flag the visibility in Console and coordinate comms with Growth/Support; show annotation and provide breakdown of 'throttled' vs 'served'.

Risk: Mapping table for model_variant may be incomplete for new model variants. Mitigation: fallback to storing original envelope and add monitoring for unmapped variants; create a short-lived task for research team to update mapping weekly during rollout.
